questions.q:
With reference to Vikram-1, launched on 18 July 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It was built by Agnikul Cosmos of Chennai.
2. All four of its stages use liquid propulsion.
3. With it, India became the first country after the US with private orbital launch capability.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None of the statements is correct. Vikram-1 was built by Skyroot Aerospace of Hyderabad; Agnikul flew a sub-orbital test. It has three solid stages and a fourth liquid stage, a restartable orbital adjustment module. With it India became the third country with private orbital launch capability, after the US and China. It carries up to 350 kg to low Earth orbit.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: 3D-printed rocket engines tend to be more reliable than engines assembled from many machined parts.
Statement-II: Additive manufacturing produces single-piece parts, removing bolts, seals and joints that can leak or fail.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first. Laser fusion of metal powder builds parts layer by layer, cutting component count and production time by about 80 per cent and allowing internal cooling channels for regenerative cooling. Skyroot's 3D-printed injector cut mass by half. Prototypes can be made in days, speeding the test-fail-redesign cycle.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a disadvantage of carbon-fibre composite rocket bodies compared with metal bodies?
o: Poor resistance to corrosion and fatigue
They cannot be made in long single pieces
Internal damage such as delamination may be hidden and needs ultrasonic inspection
questions.e: Composites are far stronger for their weight than aerospace aluminium or maraging steel, resist fatigue and corrosion, and can be laid into seamless tubes; Vikram-1's first stage is India's longest single-piece composite stage. Their drawbacks are high material and curing costs, directional strength and hidden damage, whereas a dent in aluminium is visible.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Launch vehicle : Developer or producer
1. Vikram-1 : Skyroot Aerospace
2. SSLV : Licensed to Hindustan Aeronautics Limited for production
3. Agnibaan : AgniKul Cosmos, incubated at IIT Madras
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. ISRO's Small Satellite Launch Vehicle carries about 500 kg to low Earth orbit and its production has been licensed to HAL. AgniKul of Chennai is Skyroot's domestic rival. Space start-ups have grown to over 400 since the 2020 reforms, and a private launcher turns orbit access into a market.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 5-6; Agnibaan name is static

questions.q:
With reference to GAGAN, consider the following statements:
1. It is a satellite-based augmentation system developed by ISRO and the Airports Authority of India.
2. It is an independent regional navigation system that does not depend on GPS.
3. Its signals are broadcast through geostationary satellites GSAT-8, GSAT-10 and GSAT-15.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. GAGAN augments GPS with real-time corrections and integrity information, so statement 2 describes NavIC, not GAGAN. In 2026 the DGCA carried out India's first satellite-based landing approach with GAGAN on an IndiGo A320 at Udaipur. GAGAN is interoperable with the US WAAS, Europe's EGNOS and Japan's MSAS.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: GAGAN can support aircraft landing approaches at airports without an Instrument Landing System.
Statement-II: GAGAN covers India and up to 1,500 km beyond its boundary for positioning, navigation and timing.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect. The 1,500 km coverage describes NavIC, India's independent regional navigation system. GAGAN serves civil aviation over the Indian Flight Information Region by correcting GPS, which lets airports avoid costly ground-based ILS. Its dependence on US-owned GPS is a strategic weakness.

questions.q:
With reference to the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe), consider the following statements:
1. It is headquartered in Bengaluru.
2. Its approval is now mandatory for any planned re-entry of a space object by an Indian or non-Indian entity, inside or outside Indian territory.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. IN-SPACe is an autonomous single-window agency in the Department of Space, headquartered at Ahmedabad. It acts as the interface between ISRO and non-government entities, authorising private launch vehicles, satellites and services and the sharing of ISRO facilities.

questions.q: In 2026 Japan's space agency JAXA tested a prototype reusable rocket. ISRO's demonstration related to reusable launch vehicles, RLV-LEX, showed
o: vertical landing of a first-stage booster on a barge
autonomous runway landing of a winged vehicle
recovery of a fairing by parachute
in-orbit refuelling of an upper stage
questions.e: RLV-LEX was a landing experiment in which a winged body was released from a helicopter and landed autonomously on a runway. SpaceX pioneered operational reuse of first-stage boosters with Falcon 9, and China recently achieved its first reusable landing. Reuse lowers launch costs and raises launch frequency.

questions.q:
With reference to the nuclear process-heat-based hydrogen facility inaugurated by the Department of Atomic Energy in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It uses the copper-chlorine thermochemical cycle developed by BARC.
2. It draws heat from the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam.
3. The copper-chlorine cycle works at lower temperatures than many other thermochemical routes.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The heat comes from the Fast Breeder Test Reactor at the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research, Kalpakkam, so statement 2 is wrong; the FBTR is the test bed for fuels, materials and sodium technology behind the 500 MWe PFBR. The facility is described as the world's first of its kind.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Hydrogen production route : Process
1. Steam methane reforming : Natural gas and steam react at high temperature over a catalyst
2. Electrolysis : Electricity splits water into hydrogen and oxygen
3. Photoelectrochemical splitting : Sunlight and special semiconductors split water
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. Steam methane reforming runs at 700 to 1,000 degrees Celsius and produces carbon dioxide as well, which is why it yields 'grey' hydrogen. Electrolysis with renewable power gives green hydrogen, and nuclear heat offers a carbon-free thermochemical route. Note that 'SMR' can also mean small modular reactor.

questions.q:
With reference to the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation, consider the following statements:
1. It was set up by China with headquarters in Shanghai.
2. India is one of its founding members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The inter-governmental body was formally set up on 16 July 2026 with 29 members, including Indonesia, Brazil, Russia and Pakistan; India is not a member. It is seen as China's bid to shape global AI rules and counter US restrictions on chips and AI. China's Moonshot AI released the open-weight Kimi K3 model at the same time.

questions.q: The 'AI for Good Global Commission', whose founding members include Indian business leaders, is led by the
questions.e: The ITU, the UN agency for information and communication technology, was founded in 1865 and is headquartered in Geneva; it coordinates radio spectrum and satellite orbits and sets technical standards. The commission has over 40 founding members, including heads of government, CEOs and UN agency heads, to widen access to AI and build trust.

questions.q:
With reference to India's drone initiatives, consider the following statements:
1. NIDAR 2.0 is a national innovation challenge in which students build drones powered by an Indian-made chip.
2. SwaYaan is run by the Ministry of Civil Aviation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct; the challenge is run by MeitY with Drone Federation India and has a prize pool of over Rs 65 lakh. SwaYaan, approved in 2022 with Rs 89.87 crore over five years, is also a MeitY programme; it builds a skilled drone workforce through a hub-and-spoke network of 30 premier institutions.

questions.q: 'White Rabbit' technology, used in the network inaugurated at Bengaluru for distributing Indian Standard Time, was developed by
o: the US National Institute of Standards and Technology
questions.e: White Rabbit extends Ethernet to give sub-nanosecond synchronisation, carrying time and data over one optical fibre, and is open source. The network supports the 'One Nation, One Time' initiative and proposed rules requiring official and commercial activity to follow IST, reducing reliance on GPS time that can be spoofed or jammed.

questions.q:
With reference to Indian Standard Time, consider the following statements:
1. It is based on the meridian of 82 degrees 30 minutes East, passing through Mirzapur.
2. It is maintained by CSIR-National Physical Laboratory.
3. It is five hours and thirty minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct. India lies east of Greenwich, so the sun rises earlier and IST is ahead of GMT. CSIR-NPL keeps national time with atomic clocks, and the 2026 IST Rules make its use mandatory for official and commercial systems. Precise time matters for power grids, telecom, defence, stock exchanges and digital payments.

questions.q: 'SpudCell', reported in 2026, is
o: a synthetic protocell with a fatty membrane and a small genome that can grow and replicate its genome
a solar cell made from perovskite
a lab-grown organoid of the human liver
questions.e: SpudCell has 36 genes and a 90-kilobase-pair genome, and uses the PURE cell-free protein synthesis system to feed, grow and copy its genome. It divides through mechanical stress from membrane proteins, without a cytoskeleton. It is not truly alive, since it lacks defences and waste removal and depends on external nutrients and ribosomes.

questions.q:
Under the 2026 amendment to the Drugs Rules, 1945, which of the following were brought under the Central Licence Approving Authority?
1. Cell and stem-cell-derived products
2. Gene therapeutic products
3. Xenografts
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: All three now come under the Central Licence Approving Authority, a division of CDSCO, for uniform regulation. Vaccines, large-volume parenterals and recombinant DNA medicines were already under joint central and State supervision. The first genetically modified pig heart was transplanted into a human in 2022.

questions.q:
With reference to Qdenga, approved in India in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It was developed by Bharat Biotech.
2. It is an inactivated vaccine against a single dengue serotype.
3. It has WHO prequalification.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 3 is correct. Qdenga is made by Takeda of Japan, produced in Germany, and is India's first approved dengue vaccine. It is a live, attenuated, tetravalent vaccine covering all four serotypes, built on a DENV-2 backbone and produced in Vero cells. Dengue is spread by Aedes mosquitoes, and a second infection with a different serotype can be more severe.

questions.q: Under the revised operational guidelines of Anemia Mukt Bharat, which group was added as the seventh beneficiary group?
o: Low birth weight babies aged 0 to 6 months
questions.e: The framework moved from 6x6x6 to 7x7x7: seven beneficiary groups, seven interventions and seven institutional mechanisms. Intravenous iron therapy was added, along with attention to non-nutritional causes such as malaria, haemoglobinopathies and fluorosis. Anaemia affects 67.1 per cent of children aged 6 to 59 months.

questions.q:
With reference to viral hepatitis, consider the following statements:
1. Hepatitis B and C spread mainly through the faecal-oral route.
2. A vaccine is available against hepatitis C.
3. Hepatitis D occurs only in people already infected with hepatitis B.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 3 is correct; the hepatitis B vaccine therefore also protects against D. Hepatitis A and E spread through the faecal-oral route, while B, C and D spread through blood and body fluids. There is no vaccine for hepatitis C, but it is curable in nearly all cases with direct-acting antivirals. The WHO's 2026 report flagged low testing and treatment coverage.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The WHO's 2026 progress report found the world on track to meet its 2030 targets for sexually transmitted infections.
Statement-II: Antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae is described as a critical threat.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct. The report found the world off track: syphilis and gonorrhoea are rising and resistant gonorrhoea is a critical threat. HIV showed progress, with new infections down 42 per cent and AIDS deaths down 57 per cent, though 9 million people still lack antiretroviral therapy.

questions.q:
With reference to NITI Aayog's 'Strategic Roadmap for Making Ayurveda Global', consider the following statements:
1. Ayurveda is included in Module 2 of the WHO's International Classification of Diseases (ICD-11).
2. Most qualified Ayurveda practitioners work outside India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct; Module 2 codes traditional-medicine conditions. About 95 per cent of India's 3.55 lakh qualified practitioners stay in India, which limits global reach. Exports doubled to about 2.16 billion dollars in 2023. Recommendations include a global Ayurveda register, WHO-GMP upgrades and 'Ayush visa' packages for medical travel.
